title: Best Travel Insurance for Seniors 2026: 5 Plans Compared
description: We compared 5 travel insurance plans for seniors 60+. Best overall: Allianz OneTrip Prime. Medical limits, cancel-for-any-reason, and pre-existing coverage ranked.
lede: Travel insurance for seniors isn't about worst-case thinking — it's about traveling confidently when the stakes are higher. A trip interruption at 35 costs a flight change fee; at 68 it can mean a $40,000 medical evacuation. The five plans below were evaluated specifically on what matters most after 60: high medical limits, solid pre-existing condition coverage, emergency evacuation, and policies that don't bury the exclusions in fine print.

sections.heading: How to Choose Senior Travel Insurance
paragraphs: Most standard travel insurance was designed for healthy 30-year-olds. Seniors need to look past the trip cancellation headline number and scrutinize the medical limits, pre-existing condition waiver rules, and what counts as a covered evacuation. A plan that looks cheap may exclude the exact scenarios that are most likely.

subsections.heading: Medical Coverage Limits
paragraphs: Aim for at least $100,000 in emergency medical coverage when traveling internationally. Medical care abroad — particularly in the US if you're visiting from elsewhere, or in European private hospitals — runs $5,000–$20,000 per day for serious conditions. Some plans cap at $50,000; that's not enough for a cardiac event requiring hospitalization.

subsections.heading: Pre-Existing Condition Waivers
paragraphs: Most plans exclude pre-existing conditions by default. The workaround is a 'pre-existing condition waiver,' which you qualify for by purchasing within 14–21 days of your first trip deposit. Miss that window and a flare-up of a managed condition (diabetes, heart disease, hypertension) may not be covered. Check the look-back period — some plans examine 60 days of medical history, others 180.

subsections.heading: Emergency Medical Evacuation
paragraphs: Medical evacuation by air ambulance from a remote location or a country with limited medical facilities costs $15,000–$100,000. Look for plans with $500,000+ in evacuation coverage. Some plans include 'return home after hospitalization' — this covers commercial transport home after stabilization, which is distinct from emergency evacuation.

subsections.heading: Cancel for Any Reason (CFAR)
paragraphs: Standard cancel-for-covered-reasons policies cover illness, death of a family member, weather disruptions, and similar. Cancel for Any Reason upgrades reimburse 50–75% of trip cost if you cancel for any reason at all — including simply changing your mind. CFAR typically costs 40–60% more than the base premium and must be added at purchase. For seniors with uncertain health, it's worth the premium.

sections.heading: Bottom line
paragraphs: Allianz OneTrip Prime is the workhorse — widely available, solid medical limits, and an easy pre-existing condition waiver process. GeoBlue is the choice for travelers who prioritize medical quality access (direct billing to providers globally) over the lowest premium. Seven Corners is best for budget-conscious seniors who travel domestically or to low-cost medical destinations. For comprehensive trip protection including cancel-for-any-reason, AIG Travel Guard Gold is worth the premium.

faqs.q: Is there an age limit on travel insurance for seniors?
faqs.a: Most plans cover travelers up to age 80. Some extend to 85 or higher, while others impose higher premiums or reduced benefits after certain ages. GeoBlue and Seven Corners are generally more accommodating of older travelers. Always check the maximum issue age before purchasing.

Original Medicare (Parts A and B) does not cover medical care outside the United States except in very limited circumstances near the US-Canada or US-Mexico border. Medicare Advantage plans may offer some international emergency coverage, but it's usually capped low. Dedicated travel insurance is the practical solution for international trips.

faqs.q: What is a look-back period in travel insurance?
faqs.a: The look-back period is how far back an insurer examines your medical history to determine what counts as a pre-existing condition. A 60-day look-back is more favorable to travelers than a 180-day look-back. Conditions treated or consulted about during the look-back window may be excluded without a waiver.

faqs.q: When should I buy travel insurance?
faqs.a: As soon as you make your first trip deposit — typically within 14–21 days to qualify for the pre-existing condition waiver. Earlier purchase also means more covered reasons for cancellation (a condition diagnosed after purchase but before travel may be covered; one diagnosed before purchase won't be).

faqs.q: Does travel insurance cover trip cancellation due to a health condition?
faqs.a: Standard plans cover cancellation if a doctor certifies you're medically unfit to travel due to an unforeseen illness or injury. They generally won't cover cancellation due to a pre-existing condition flare-up unless you purchased a pre-existing condition waiver. Cancel for Any Reason coverage is the only option that removes this restriction entirely.

products.review: Allianz OneTrip Prime is the standard recommendation for a reason: $100,000 in medical coverage, $1 million in emergency evacuation, pre-existing condition waiver available within 14 days of deposit, and 24/7 assistance that's actually reachable. The pre-existing condition waiver window is shorter than some competitors (14 days vs. 21), so purchase quickly after booking. Trip cancellation and interruption limits are solid for most trip costs. Pricing from $42 per trip is fair for the coverage offered.
pros: $1 million emergency evacuation — sufficient for most scenarios
Pre-existing condition waiver with reasonable requirements
24/7 assistance line has strong user reviews for responsiveness
cons: 14-day waiver window is tighter than some competitors
CFAR not available on all plans

products.review: AIG Travel Guard Gold is the plan for travelers who want maximum flexibility, including Cancel for Any Reason at 75% reimbursement — one of the highest CFAR percentages available. Medical limits reach $100,000 with evacuation at $500,000. Pre-existing condition waiver available within 15 days of initial deposit. The premium reflects the coverage: at $55+ per trip it's not the budget pick, but for seniors with complex health situations or expensive trips, the coverage depth is worth it.
pros: CFAR at 75% — highest reimbursement rate on this list
Strong trip cancellation and interruption limits
cons: Medical limits lower than GeoBlue for medical-only travelers

products.review: Nationwide Prime shines on trip cancellation and interruption: up to 100% and 150% of trip cost respectively, which covers non-refundable deposits and the cost of getting home mid-trip. Medical coverage at $75,000 is adequate for most destinations but lower than Allianz or GeoBlue. Pre-existing condition waiver available within 21 days — the most generous window on this list. Pricing from $49 sits in the middle of the range.
pros: 150% trip interruption coverage — the best ratio here
21-day pre-existing waiver window gives more flexibility
cons: $75,000 medical limit — lower than top competitors
Evacuation coverage capped lower than Allianz

products.review: Seven Corners RoundTrip starts at $38, making it the most affordable plan on this list. For domestic trips or travel to countries with lower medical costs, the coverage is adequate. For extended international trips, the medical limits are the weak point — $100,000 max on higher tiers, but base plans start lower. The 20-day pre-existing condition waiver window is reasonable. Customer service reviews are mixed, which matters when you actually need to file a claim.
pros: Most affordable starting premium on this list
Good for short domestic trips or budget international travel
cons: Customer service reviews less consistent than Allianz
Lower tier plans have reduced medical limits

products.review: GeoBlue Voyager Choice is a medical-first plan built for travelers who prioritize healthcare quality over everything else. The medical network includes premium hospitals in 190+ countries with direct billing — no out-of-pocket upfront costs at network providers. Medical limits reach $1 million. The trade-off is that trip cancellation coverage is limited compared to general travel insurance plans. At $56+, it's priced for travelers whose primary concern is what happens if they get seriously ill abroad.
pros: $1 million medical coverage — best on this list
Direct billing at 190+ country network — no upfront costs
Strong for extended trips and medical-risk travelers
cons: Trip cancellation coverage weaker than Allianz or AIG

methodology: Plans were evaluated on medical coverage limits, emergency evacuation limits, pre-existing condition waiver availability and window, cancel-for-any-reason options, customer service quality, and price-to-coverage ratio specifically for travelers 60 and older. We did not test these products ourselves.
pinDescription: Don't travel without the right coverage. These 5 senior travel insurance plans are ranked on medical limits, pre-existing conditions, and what actually gets paid when you need it.
